tasks.short: Model social behaviour and encourage concern for others

steps.what: Model appropriate social behaviours and encourage concern for others during everyday interactions

tasks.design: Keep social modelling and encouragement with the nanny. Existing family guidance in {DOCS} may inform practice, but no behavioural scoring or automated relationship intervention is added.
tasks.previous_blocker: Children learn from how a trusted adult responds in the moment.
tasks.enabler_now: No software change is needed for the unchanged interaction.
tasks.still_hard: Responding consistently to different children and social situations.
tasks.human_edge: Show care, patience and respectful communication through actual behaviour.
tasks.altitude: Direct interaction time and care responsibilities stay unchanged.

reach.task: Reflect on a recurring social difficulty with the caregiver

evidence.claim: Modelling social behaviour is live relational work retained with the caregiver in this design.

assumptions: Boundary is everyday modelling and encouragement, not assessment, diagnosis or creating a behaviour plan.
The nanny hears and observes interactions during s1 with all time retained. No structured social score, emotion inference or machine action is used.
Native access to existing guidance is sufficient. Zero incremental upkeep because no new tool, content or record process is introduced.
research_questions: Which situations call for a consistent human response rather than additional instructions?

already_counted.description: Model behaviour and support social interaction

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100, R=100 and net zero. All modelling and interaction remain; no saving from replacing adult attention is assumed.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Organise and conduct age-appropriate recreational activities

steps.what: Choose age-appropriate games, crafts, sports, walks or play dates for the children
Organise materials, location and practical arrangements for the recreational activity
Conduct recreational activities and adapt play, walks or games to children's responses

tasks.design: Retain practical activity choice, preparation and participation with the nanny. Existing family arrangements in {CALENDAR} can remain a reference without introducing an assumed lesson-writing step.
tasks.previous_blocker: Most organisation is choosing something suitable and getting children, materials and space ready.
tasks.enabler_now: No new software is required for the proposed unchanged activity.
tasks.still_hard: Changing weather, energy, interests and individual participation needs.
tasks.human_edge: Notice when to simplify, extend or stop an activity for the actual children present.
tasks.altitude: Recreation time and responsibility stay unchanged.

reach.task: Adapt a game for children with different participation needs
reach.learn: Inclusive play and safe material selection

evidence.claim: Activity generation is distinct from organising materials and conducting responsive play; this design retains the latter work.

assumptions: Boundary includes everyday practical organisation and live activity, not formal lesson plans, ticket purchasing or travel booking.

Nanny chooses the activity from direct knowledge in s1 and checks existing permissions in s2 with all time retained. New permission is sought manually when needed; no structured approval flag or free family capture is assumed.
All material preparation and child supervision remain. Native calendar access is sufficient and no build is proposed.
Zero incremental upkeep because no new activity library, data collection or automation is introduced.
unknowns: Usual activity range and family permissions
research_questions: Is significant repeated clerical coordination present beyond physical preparation and direct activity choice?

already_counted.description: Choose, prepare and conduct recreational activities

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100, R=100 and net zero. Retain practical organisation and all live activity; no invented planning-document baseline is removed.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Assign suitable chores and encourage responsibility

steps.what: Assign appropriate chores matched to the child's ability and the family routine
Guide the chore and praise targeted behaviours to encourage self-control, confidence and responsibility

tasks.design: Keep chore choice, guidance and specific encouragement with the nanny. A family routine in {DOCS} can remain a reference without automated behaviour tracking or reward allocation.
tasks.previous_blocker: Appropriate responsibility depends on what the child can manage today and how support is offered.
tasks.enabler_now: No new technology is needed for this unchanged interaction.
tasks.still_hard: Providing help without taking over and praising effort appropriately.
tasks.human_edge: Notice a child's effort and give encouragement that fits the moment.
tasks.altitude: Chore guidance time and care judgement stay unchanged.

reach.task: Agree consistent encouragement around a shared routine
reach.learn: Developmentally appropriate responsibility and supportive prompts

evidence.claim: Choosing suitable chores and giving meaningful encouragement are contextual human interactions retained in this design.

assumptions: Boundary is the nanny's guidance and encouragement; the child's own chore time is not labour saved by the nanny.
Nanny observes readiness and effort directly in the retained steps. No structured behaviour score, automated reward or inferred self-confidence is produced.
Existing family guidance is sufficient. Zero incremental upkeep because no new chart, app or data collection is introduced.
research_questions: Which chores require direct support or adaptation for the child?

already_counted.description: Choose chores, support practice and offer specific encouragement

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100, R=100 and net zero. Retain assignment judgement and encouragement; no saving is created by shifting household work to the child.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Observe health concerns and provide directed care or transport

steps.what: Observe children's behaviour for irregularities, take temperature when appropriate and communicate concerns
Administer medications only as directed and within existing authorisation, or seek clarification
Transport children to the doctor when directed and hand over relevant observations

tasks.design: Retain health observation, directed medication care and physical transport with the nanny under existing authorisations. Instructions in {DOCS} remain the source; no automated diagnosis, dose choice or clinical recommendation is introduced.
tasks.previous_blocker: The task combines observation, role limits and physical care that records do not replace.
tasks.enabler_now: No technology change or additional medical authority is assumed.
tasks.still_hard: Knowing what is authorised, recognising uncertainty and contacting the responsible person promptly.
tasks.human_edge: Observe the child directly, verify instructions and provide calm practical support.
tasks.altitude: Care and transport time stay unchanged, with no new diagnostic or prescribing rights.

reach.task: Clarify the caregiver's authorised health-care and escalation arrangements
reach.learn: Instruction verification, care limits and factual handover

evidence.claim: Direct observation, authorised medication care and transporting a child remain human and physical work in this design.

assumptions: Boundary is care already within the nanny's training and local authority, plus directed transport. Clinical diagnosis, prescribing and the doctor's own work are outside it.
Shares represent an illustrative mix of alternatives over many cases, not a rule to medicate and transport every child. No treatment sequence or medical decision rule is supplied.

Nanny produces actual observations in s1 and checks current instructions directly in s2 with full time retained. Authorised parent or clinician supplies the existing medication instruction and transport direction outside this task; their unchanged communication time earns no saving.
Unclear or missing instructions lead to human clarification under the existing care procedure. No structured health flag, machine triage or automated medication action is used.
Native document access is sufficient. Zero incremental upkeep because no new care tool, recording process or clinical logic is introduced.
unknowns: Local care authorisations and nanny training
research_questions: Can the nanny identify the current authorised instruction and responsible contact without relying on memory?

already_counted.description: Observe health, provide permitted directed care and complete directed transport

incremental.description: No added automation or care-process upkeep

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100, R=100 and net zero. All observation, instruction checking, physical care and transport remain. No saving is claimed from moving responsibility to a parent or clinician.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: The nanny's direct care, activity organisation, encouragement and health-support responsibilities remain unchanged.
reach: Reflect on care routines with childcare supervision
Use clear factual handovers to responsible health professionals
role.ambitious_version: A caregiver who supports children consistently and knows when to ask the responsible person for guidance; these tasks have no demonstrated clerical saving.
